layout_dets.text: Abstract: This paper presents a novel method for the automatic segmentation of coronary arteries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in X-ray angiograms, based on multiscale analysis and neural networks. The multiscale analysis is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performed by using Gaussian filters in the spatial domain and Gabor filters in the frequency domain,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which are used as inputs by a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for the enhancement of vessel-like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures. The optimal design of the MLP is selected following a statistical comparative analysis,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using a training set of 100 angiograms, and the area under the ROC curve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for assessment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the detection performance. The detection results of the proposed method are compared with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eleven state-of-the-art blood vessel enhancement methods, obtaining the highest performance of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , with a test set of 30 angiograms. The database of 130 X-ray coronary angiograms has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been outlined by a specialist and approved by a medical ethics committee. On the other hand, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel extraction technique was selected from fourteen binary classification algorithms applied to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the multiscale filter response. Finally, the proposed segmentation method is compared with twelve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state-of-the-art vessel segmentation methods in terms of six binary evaluation metrics, where the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed method provided the most accurate coronary arteries segmentation with a classification

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rate of 0.9698 and Dice coefficient of 0.6857, using the test set of angiograms. In addition to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experimental results, the performance in the detection and segmentation steps of the proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method have also shown that it can be highly suitable for systems that perform computer-aided

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diagnosis in X-ray imaging.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Keywords: automatic segmentation; coronary arteries; medical imaging; multiscale Gabor filters;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Multiscale Gaussian Filters; multilayer perceptron

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The task of automatic segmentation of coronary arteries in X-ray angiograms can be integrated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in a computer-aided diagnosis system (CAD) to support the analysis of coronary heart disease.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In cardiology, the X-ray coronary angiogram is the gold standard employed to evaluate and monitor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: abnormalities of the coronary arteries. However, the detection of blood vessels in coronary angiograms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is a challenging task for the current CAD systems. The most common problems that are present

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in coronary angiograms involve the non-uniform illumination, weak contrast between arterial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: www.mdpi.com/journal/applsci

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 of 27

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: features and image background, and occlusion caused by different organs or medical devices in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the acquired images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the literature, the challenge of automatic detection of blood vessels has been widely addressed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by different methods. A common approach is the use of operators and transformations from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mathematical morphology framework. The most used strategy to enhance vessel-like structures is the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Top-hat operator, which was applied by Eiho and Qian [1] in coronary angiograms. The Top-hat

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: response is combined with an interactive procedure to segment the main artery using another

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: morphological operator. Later, a multiscale approach composed for the Top-hat filter responses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a number of structuring elements at different size was proposed by Qian et al. [2]. This method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: allows the automatic detection of vessels with different diameters in a single medical image.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Other common methodology is based on the information of the Hessian matrix of the medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image. In this approach, the gradient of an image is defined as the convolution of itself and the first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: order derivative of a Gaussian curve. Consequently, the Hessian matrix of the image is the second order

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: derivative of a Gaussian curve convolved with the image. Frangi et al. [3] proposed the enhancement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of tubular structures, such is the case of blood vessels, by using a vesselness measure defined from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix. For the particular problem of detection of coronary arteries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in X-ray angiograms, multiple vesselness measures have been recently proposed. Wang et al. [4]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used the eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix to construct a vessel probability map; in a similar manner,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Li et al. [5] proposed the generation of a vessel feature map also from the Hessian matrix using a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different vesselness measure. These two works use the vessel map as starting point for a region

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: growing method to segment the coronary artery tree.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: On the other hand, methods based on matching templates have considered the shape of a blood

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel in the spatial domain to propose a suitable model. Chaudhuri et al. [6] introduced a two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dimensional Gaussian Matched Filter (GMF) for the enhancement of blood vessels in retinal fundus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images. GMF is founded under the fact that in the spatial domain the cross-section of a blood vessel is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Gaussian shaped. In addition, GMF assumes that vessels can be modeled in segments that share the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same orientation and diameter. To detect vessel segments at different orientations, a directional filter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bank is built by rotating the GMF template into a number of evenly spaced directions in the range

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to be later convolved with the input image. Methods based on the GMF have modified

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the parameters that govern the shape of the matching template and the number of orientations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Most of them have selected the parameters empirically, such is the case of the method proposed by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cinsdikici and Aydın [7], where the number of directional templates is increased in order to improve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the detection performance. In the method proposed by Kang et al. [8], the parameters were empirically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modified to allow the detection of arteries in coronary angiograms. Moreover, some methods have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addressed the selection of the parameters by a training step prior to its application. A first approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is the proposed by Al-Rawi et al. [9], where a full-search of the parameters was employed. Later,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Al-Rawi and Karajeh [10] proposed a method from the Evolutionary Computation algorithms (EC)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to reduce the computational time consumed by the exhaustive search. More recently, Cruz et al. [11]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performed a study to determine the most suitable EC method for the automatic selection of parameters

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the GMF applied to the coronary artery segmentation problem.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An alternative to the analysis of the image in the spatial domain is the use of Gabor filters in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the frequency domain. Gabor filters for blood vessel enhancement in medical images was proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by Soares et al. [12] based on its capability of detecting oriented features. Similarly to GMF, Gabor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: filters can be rotated into different directions in order to detect vessel-like structures in multiple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: orientations. An important modification to the Gabor filter was proposed by Rangayyan et al. [13],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where a simplified definition of the filter is presented, in addition to the use of only the real part of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: filter, discarding the imaginary part which is commonly used to detect edge features. For Gabor filters,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recent methods have been proposed to select the most appropriate parameters for the detection of blood

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels in image data. The method proposed by Rangayyan et al. [13,14] performs a full-search for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the parameters of elongation, average width, and number of oriented filters before selecting the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 of 27

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suitable values for the detection of blood vessels in retinal fundus images. Later, Cervantes et al. [15]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed the use of a Boltzmann based EC algorithm for the automatic selection of the Gabor filter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters for the coronary artery segmentation problem.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Considering that the filter responses obtained by the blood vessel detection methods can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: treated as multilevel classifiers, the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve analysis (ROC) has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frequently used to evaluate and compare their vessel detection efficiency.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Gabor filters have shown the best detection performance in coronary arteries compared to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state-of-the-art approaches [15,16], followed in efficiency by the Gaussian matched filters [11]. Because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these two methods have obtained superior performance to carry out the automatic detection of blood

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels in medical images, in this work they are thoroughly studied. However, it is important to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: point out that coronary arteries present a natural variant thickness along their span; consequently,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a multiscale approach is convenient in order to enhance vessel-like structures properly.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper a novel method that uses the multiscale filter responses of the GMF and Gabor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: filters to improve the detection of coronary arteries in X-ray angiograms is presented. The proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method addresses the limitation that single-scale versions of the GMF and Gabor filters present when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhancing vessel-like structures of a unique thickness at a time. In the method, a multilayer perceptron

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network (MLP) is fed with the multiscale filter responses of the GMF and Gabor filters methods in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: order to obtain an improved detection response using information from the spatial and frequency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domains of the X-ray image.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In addition, to select the optimal MLP configuration for detecting coronary arteries, a hypothesis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test for stochastic domination between multiple possible architectures has been performed. To evaluate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the detection step of the proposed method, eleven methods for blood vessel enhancement are compared

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the proposed method in terms of the area under the ROC curve. Finally, in the segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: step of the proposed method, twelve specialized blood vessel segmentation methods are used for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comparative analysis in terms of six binary classification metrics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The organization of this paper is the following. In Section 2, the basis of the Gaussian matched

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: filters, Gabor filters and Artificial Neural Networks, along with the proposed method including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiscale analysis, are described in detail. Computational experiments including numerical and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: qualitative results are discussed in Section 3, and finally, the concluding remarks can be found in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 4.

layout_dets.text: 2. Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this section, the single-scale and multiscale versions of the Gaussian matched filters and Gabor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: filters are described first in Sections 2.1 and 2.2. Later, an introduction to Artificial Neural Networks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that are used by the proposed method to perform the multiscale analysis of the coronary angiograms is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: given in Section 2.3. Additionally, the proposed method and the metrics used to evaluate its detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and segmentation performance can be found in Sections 2.4 and 2.5, respectively.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1. Multiscale Gaussian Matched Filters

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Gaussian matched filters were proposed for vessel enhancement in medical images of the retina [6].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The original GMF method follows the assumption that a vessel cross-section can be approximated by a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: single-scaled Gaussian curve. Moreover, this method considers that blood vessels can be studied as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: individual segments that share a similar orientation and diameter, and consequently can be detected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with matching templates. In the detection process of the GMF, the vessel structures are enhanced by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the convolution of the original image with a gray-scale template defined under a Gaussian distribution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: After filtering, the vessel detection response shows an increased contrast between vessel-like structures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the image background. The main idea behind the GMF is supported by the single-scale Gaussian

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 2.2. Multiscale Gabor Filters

layout_dets.text: 2.3. Artificial Neural Networks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is a machine learning technique consisting on the assembly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of multiple processing units called neurons. ANN are capable of replicate the behavior of unknown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: functions as universal function approximators [19]. A common function to replicate by an ANN is the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: judgment of an expert during image labeling, which could be considered as a classification problem.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In classification problems, the prediction process of an artificial neural network could be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpreted as a sequence of projections into new feature spaces, where the linear separation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: patterns represents a simpler task. In the projection sequence, each neuron performs a weighted sum of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its corresponding inputs; in addition, a bias term is frequently employed to center the neuron response

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: around a decision boundary.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In order to simulate the biological activation of the neuron, a function is applied to the resulting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neuron response. The asymptotic behavior of the activation of a neuron is commonly approximated by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a nonlinear step function, such as hyperbolic tangent and sigmoid functions. Moreover, differentiable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: activation functions are selected when gradient-based methods are used for the optimization of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: artificial neural network parameters.

layout_dets.text: The classification performance of an ANN can be increased by adding more neurons to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: given the large possible neuron arrangements. Layered configurations are a particular arrangement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the ANN neurons, where the computing units apply the same transfer function and share the input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data. Moreover, layers of neurons can be connected to other layers, being the Multilayer Perceptron

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 3.2. MLP Architecture Selection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In order to determine the optimal Multilayer perceptron architecture, the number of layers plays an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: essential role. In general, the input and output layers are directly related with the nature of the problem

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to be solved. The main challenge is given to establish the number of hidden layers along with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: number of hidden neurons for each of them. To establish the number of hidden layers in the proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Multilayer perceptron, the range of hidden layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was explored. MLP architectures with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more than two hidden layers present low performance in terms of the area under ROC curve and high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel segmentation from the single-scale GMF response. The binary segmentation is obtained by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: selecting the threshold value that maximizes the local entropy computed from the co-occurrence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matrix. Kang et al. [8] applies two different enhancement methods to the original image: the Top-hat

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operator, and the single-scale GMF. The segmentation result is obtained with a threshold level that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maximizes the entropy of the gray-scale intensity of each detection response. The method proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by Kang et al. [38] introduces a segmentation procedure based on a similarity degree between pixels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the gray-scale detection response. The approach of Nguyen et al. [25] segments vessel pixels from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the multiline detector response by using a fixed threshold value of 0.56. The value is selected as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: binarization level that maximizes the classification accuracy using a training set of images. The method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Li et al. [5] defines a vessel probability map from a coronary angiogram using a Hessian matrix

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based method. The vessel segmentation is performed by a region growing algorithm and a subsequent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel detail repairing procedure. The inter-class variance maximization method of Otsu [26] has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an efficient separation tool employed by the following methods. The method of Cervantes et al. [15]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: employs the single-scale Gabor filter, which parameters are selected using a nature inspired algorithm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for numerical optimization. The U-Net [39] is a convolutional neural network that has been widely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used for biomedical image segmentation tasks in recent years. For the comparative analysis, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: U-Net [39] was trained using the training set of 100 images, by taking patches of size 32 × 32 pixels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the zero-padded angiograms as inputs, and using the cross entropy function as loss metric.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Finally, the method proposed by Cruz et al. [17] introduced the multiscale GMF that improves the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection performance of its single-scale version.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The result of the comparative analysis of the twelve specialized vessel segmentation methods,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the proposed method, is presented in Table 5. The test set of 30 angiograms is used to evaluate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation methods in terms of binary classification accuracy. According to Table 5, the proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method obtains the highest segmentation performance with respect to the twelve methods from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state of the art by reaching a classification accuracy of 0.9698. The resulting segmentation responses of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the comparative segmentation methods are illustrated in Figure 11.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: By visual inspection of Figure 11, it can be noticed that the method of GMF/Local Entropy [37]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presents responses with a high rate of false positive pixels, obtaining the lowest segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy of the comparison, this problem is also reflected in the low positive predictive value.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The method of GMF/Degree-based [38] can obtain a relative high number of false negative pixels,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: affecting the segmentation accuracy and sensitivity of the method. The method based on single-scale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Gabor filters [15] presents a frequent problem on the resulting image edges reducing the sensitivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the method. The high false positive rate in those areas is associated to the strong detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensities obtained by using only the average vessel width as single scale. In the method based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on multiscale Gaussian templates [17], the accuracy and positive predictive value are affected by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the incorrect classification of the pixels that are closer to the main coronary artery. This problem

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is because of the strong detection responses obtained by the multiscale Gaussian matched filter for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small tubular structures in the background. The methods Hessian Matrix-based/Vessel Repair [5],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Multiline Detector/Threshold (0.56) [25] achieve similar classification accuracy. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their segmentation performance is affected by the presence of irregular edges, holes, and broken

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels, being the method of Hessian Matrix-based/Vessel Repair [5] the most affected between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both, reducing its segmentation sensitivity. The methods Top-hat/Background Unification [1], and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Multiscale Top-hat/Background Unification [2] achieve high classification accuracy, only limited

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by the frequent presence of irregular borders and broken vessels in the segmentation result

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which reduces their positive predictive value and Dice similarity coefficient with the ground-truth.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The U-Net (Ronneberger et al.) [39] method presents the highest specificity and positive predictive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: value; however, the segmentation result show a high rate of false negative pixels in several images,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resulting in broken vessels and a reduction of its overall vessel extraction performance. The method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of GMF/Entropy Maximization [8] presents high segmentation results in overall, being affected only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by the presence of holes, broken vessels, and false positives in image edges, reducing its positive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predictive value. On the other hand, the experimental results obtained by the proposed method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieved the highest segmentation accuracy, specificity, positive predictive value, and Dice similarity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coefficient, using the testing set of the present database. Because of the suitable performance of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed method, the segmented coronary arteries present a low rate of false positives along with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low presence of holes and isolated vessels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The comparison of the average execution time of the proposed method, and twelve vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation methods from the state of the art, is presented in Table 6. The methods of GMF/Entropy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Maximization [8] and GMF/Degree-based [38] present the lowest computational times, followed by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods Top-hat/Background Unification [1] and GMF/Local Entropy [37], which low computational

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time can be attributed to the single-scale analysis performed in the detection step. The methods of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Multiscale Top-hat/Background Unification [2] and Multiline Detector/Threshold (0.56) [25] employ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a multiscale analysis during the detection step, which increases the execution time with respect to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: single-scale approaches. The Single-scale Gabor filters/Otsu [15] involve transformations between the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: space and frequency domain that affects the overall execution time. The Multiscale GMF/Otsu [17]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method performs a multiscale analysis in the spatial domain, which demand a greater execution time

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than other single-scale GMF methods. The Hessian Matrix-based/Vessel Repair [5] method employs a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiscale approach during the detection step, and a vessel repair process in the segmentation step.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This method requires a greater execution time than other multiscale methods and is reflected on its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: average execution time. The proposed method presents the highest execution time in the comparative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a trade-off for its high segmentation accuracy. The computational time demanded by the proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method is directly related to the number of multiple scales of the Gaussian filter applied in the spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain and the Gabor filters performed in the frequency domain.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Finally, it is important to point out that the proposed method for the automatic segmentation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coronary arteries achieved the most accurate results using the present database and different evaluation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metrics for each of the vessel detection and segmentation steps. The high segmentation accuracy can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be attributed to the multiscale analysis performed in both spatial and frequency domains along with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the statistically determined artificial neural network. In addition, given the efficiency obtained by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed method and the competitive computational time, it could be integrated into a computer-aided

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diagnosis system to support cardiologist during the decision-making process.

layout_dets.text: 4. Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, a new method for automatic segmentation of coronary arteries, based on multiscale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analysis of X-ray angiograms, has been introduced. The proposed method employs the multiscale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Gaussian matched filters, applied in the image domain, and the multiscale Gabor filter, applied in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frequency domain, in order to improve the contrast between vessel features and background, suppress

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noise in the image, and homogenize the illumination of the angiogram. Both multiscale responses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are used as input layer in a four layered perceptron network. A statistical analysis has shown that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Multilayer perceptron with 9 neurons in each of the two hidden layers is the appropriate using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a comparative set of configurations. Moreover, the proposed method based on an artificial neural

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network with multiscale analysis has performed better than eleven vessel detection methods from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the state of the art by reaching an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when applied to 30 test images. The use of a fixed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: threshold value of 0.87, over the multiscale response of the proposed method, has proved to be the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: appropriate from fourteen segmentation techniques. Finally, according to comparative experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with twelve state-of-the-art vessel segmentation methods, the proposed method has provided the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: most accurate vessel segmentation of the test set of 30 angiograms with a classification accuracy of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.9698, and Dice coefficient of 0.6857. In addition to the experimental results, the high performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and robustness in the detection and segmentation steps have shown that the proposed method could

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be a potential method to be integrated in a computer decision support system to aid diagnosis in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical practice.
